Add two lettuce leaves to each sandwich; top with 2nd bread slice.
contributor: Produce for Better Health Foundation

title: Grapefruit Spinach Salad
ingredientLines: 4 1/2 cups fresh spinach, washed and drained
1 can sliced mushrooms, drained (2 ounce cans)
1 cup water chestnuts, diced (5 oz can)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Tear spinach coarsely and place in large salad bowl.
Add mushrooms, water chestnuts, and grapefruit.
Mix together oil, vinegar, grapefruit juice, soy sauce, hot pepper sauce, salt, and dry mustard.
Toss dressing with spinach mixture and serve.
contributor: North Dakota State University Extension Service

title: Greek Salad
ingredientLines: 6 romaine lettuces leaves (torn into 1 1/2 inch pieces)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine lettuce, cucumber, tomato, onion, and cheese in large serving bowl. Whisk together oil, lemon juice, oregano, and salt in small bowl.
Pour over lettuce mixture; toss until coated. Serve immediately.
contributor: Healthy Recipes, Adapted from Easy Greek Salad Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

title: Greek Salad with Chicken
ingredientLines: 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes, cut in half
1/4 cup black olives, cut in half
steps: To make the dressing, add Greek yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper to a small bowl. Mix well to combine.
Cover dressing and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Wash lettuce and tear into bite-sized pieces. Place in large salad bowl and add tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion, olives, and chicken.
Sprinkle with feta cheese.
Top with yogurt dressing and enjoy.
contributor: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

title: Green Beans and New Potatoes
ingredientLines: 3 1/2 cups frozen green beans (16 oz bag)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add all ingredients to a large stock pot and cover with water.
Bring to a boil and reduce to medium heat.
Cook until green beans and potatoes are tender.
contributor: Healthy Cookbook for African American Populations

title: Grilled Asparagus and Shrimp Quinoa Salad with Lemon Vinaigrette
ingredientLines: 2 cups fresh asparagus, large spears (cut into 1" pieces)
1/2 yellow or red bell pepper (cut into 1/2" pieces)
12 ounces fresh or frozen large raw shrimp (peeled and deveined)
1 1/2 cups dry quinoa (cooked according to package directions)
3 tablespoons fresh or bottled lemon juice
steps: Place vinaigrette ingredients in a small bowl and whisk; set aside.
Cut vegetables as directed.
Heat grill and grilling tray.
Place vegetables and shrimp in a large bowl; add about 1/3 of the vinaigrette (about 3 tablespoons) and toss.
Spread shrimp-vegetable mixture over hot grilling tray.
Grill, turning shrimp and vegetables, until the flesh of the shrimp is an opaque color (about 5 to 6 minutes); remove from grill.
Serve grill mixture over cooked quinoa, and drizzle with vinaigrette.
contributor: Produce for Better Health Foundation

title: Grilled Lamb Salad
ingredientLines: 12 ounces boneless leg of lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes (if cubed lamb is not available at your meat market, ask the butcher to prepare it for you)
6 cups shredded Savoy, Napa, or green cabbage
2 tablespoons black or white sesame seeds
steps: Mix marinade/dressing ingredients; divide evenly.
Place lamb cubes in a glass dish; pour half of the marinade/dressing over the lamb.
Cover and refrigerate at least two hours.
In a large bowl, toss cabbage, carrots, jicama (optional), onions, and sesame seeds.
Remove lamb and discard marinade.
Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes; divide lamb among the 4 skewers.
On hot grill, cook the lamb skewers 5 to 6 minutes per side (or to desired degree of doneness).
Remove lamb from skewers, add to salad, and toss.
To serve, divide salad evenly on four plates. Drizzle with remaining dressing.
contributor: Produce for Better Health Foundation

title: Harvest Vegetable Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine romaine lettuce and cilantro, and divide onto four plates.
Place parsnips, carrots, and turnips into 1 quart of boiling water. Return water to a simmer, cook vegetables for 2 minutes. Strain into a colander.
Mix ingredients for the dressing right before use.
Place hot vegetables on top of greens and top with homemade dressing.
contributor: 5 A Day: Eat 5 to 9 Fruits and Vegetables US Department of Health and Human Services Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

title: Hearty Vegetable Salad with Herb Dressing
ingredientLines: 3 cups cauliflower florets (fresh or frozen, thawed)
2 cups broccoli florets (fresh or frozen, thawed)
1 can red kidney beans, low-sodium (15 1/2 ounce, drained)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In large bowl, combine all salad ingredients.
In a small jar with a tight fitting lid, combine all dressing ingredients and shake well.
Pour dressing over vegetables and stir to coat vegetables. Cover; refrigerate 1 to 4 hours to marinate, tossing occasionally.
contributor: Montana State University Extension Service

title: Herb Potato Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub potatoes and cut into cubes.
Place in medium saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 12 minutes or until potatoes are done. Drain.
Mix dressing ingredients.
Combine hot potatoes, dressing, radishes, basil, thyme, and onion powder. Serve hot or cold.
contributor: University of Nebraska Recipe Collection Staff from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln Cooperative Extension

title: Homemade Ranch Dressing
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Collect and measure all ingredients before starting to prepare the recipe.
Add the dried onion, salt, garlic powder, and dried parsley to a bowl, and stir gently to combine.
Add the Greek yogurt and buttermilk, and stir until spices are evenly distributed.
Chill before serving.
Keep leftovers refrigerated, and eat within 1 week.
contributor: Eating Smart, Being Active Colorado State University

title: Italian Pasta Salad
ingredientLines: 1/2 cup Italian salad dressing, light or reduced fat (can use more if desired)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together in a large bowl.
Refrigerate for about 30 minutes before serving.
contributor: Oregon’s Healthy Harvest Recipes Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

title: Kale Salad with Yogurt Dressing
ingredientLines: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or oil of your choice, divided)
1 lemon (zested and juiced - save zest for dressing)
1 lime (zested and juiced - save zest for dressing)
1/2 cup cilantro (chopped or torn, stems included)
1 jalapeño chile pepper (seeds removed and diced, optional)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and dry kale. Remove stems and tear into bite-sized pieces.
Season kale with salt, pepper, 1 tablespoon of olive oil, lemon juice, and lime juice.
With your hands, massage kale until the leaves just start to wilt.
Make the dressing - in a small bowl, add the salt and pepper to the yogurt.
Add the lemon and lime zest and remaining 1 tablespoon of oil.
Mix in cilantro and jalapeno pepper, if desired.
With a spoon, mix massaged kale with yogurt dressing.
Toss pumpkin seeds over salad.
contributor: USDA Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)

title: Kale with Nuts and Raisins
ingredientLines: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or oil of your choice)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 350 °F.
On a baking sheet, toast nuts for 5 minutes.
Heat oil in frying pan on medium heat.
Add garlic and kale to frying pan and cook for 4 minutes.
Add raisins and nuts and cook for 1 minute more.
Add salt to taste (optional)
contributor: Eat Smart. Be Fit. University of Maryland Extension

title: Leaf Finger Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lay lettuce leaves on a flat surface. Top each leaf with all ingredients: cucumbers, carrots, beets, and sunflower seeds.
Drizzle each leaf with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Slowly roll the leaf with all ingredients.
contributor: University of California at Davis Children's Garden Program

title: Lentil Vegetable Salad
ingredientLines: 2 cups potatoes, sliced (15 ounce can, low-sodium)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil 1 cup water in a saucepan.
Add the lentils. Cook for 20 minutes over low heat until tender, then drain.
Cook the peas for 3 minutes in another saucepan. Then remove from heat.
Rinse and drain the peas.
Wash, peel, and shred the carrots.
Put the cooked lentils, sliced potatoes, peas, and shredded carrots in a bowl.
Put the parsley, vinegar, mustard, and olive oil in another bowl. Stir well.
Pour the dressing over the lentil vegetable salad.
contributor: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

title: Magical Fruit Salad
ingredientLines: 1 can (20 ounces) pineapple chunks, juice packed
1 cup seedless grapes, red or green
1 package (3.5 ounces) instant pudding mix, lemon or vanilla
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain off the juice from the canned pineapples. Put chunks in a large bowl.
Rinse the grapes and drain. Add the grapes to the bowl.
Peel the bananas and cut into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl.
Pour the milk over the fruit. While slowly stirring the fruit mixture, sprinkle in the pudding mix.
Let the mixture stand for 5 minutes and serve.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
contributor: Food Hero Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

title: Mango Berry Rotini Salad
ingredientLines: 1 cup (4 oz) whole-wheat rotini pasta, uncooked
steps: In a small bowl, whisk vinaigrette ingredients; set aside.
Boil water and cook rotini according to package instructions. Drain cooked rotini and rinse in cool water.
While rotini is cooking, cut mango into chunks, removing peel and pit.
Place salad ingredients in a large bowl; drizzle with vinaigrette. Toss gently.
contributor: Produce for Better Health Foundation

title: Marinated Three-Bean Salad
ingredientLines: 1/2 can cut green beans, low-sodium (8 ounce)
1/2 can red kidney beans, low-sodium (8 ounce)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain the canned beans.
Peel and chop the onion.
In a large bowl, combine the cannellini beans, green beans, kidney beans, onion, and celery.
Pour the Italian dressing over the vegetables and toss lightly.
Cover the bowl and marinate in the refrigerator for at least one hour. The salad can be left in the refrigerator over night.
Drain before serving.
contributor: The Texas A&M University System Texas Cooperative Extension Expanded Nutrition Program

title: Mediterranean Chicken and White Bean Salad
ingredientLines: 1 cup skinless cooked chicken (diced into 1/2 inch pieces)
1 can 15.5 ounce low-sodium white beans (drained and rinsed with cold water)
1 cucumber (peeled and diced into 1/2 inch pieces)
1/4 red or white onion (peeled and chopped into 1/2 inch pieces)
1 tablespoon dried basil or parsley leaves
steps: Put everything in the bowl and gently toss.
Serve right away, or cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days.
contributor: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

title: Mediterranean Tuna Antipasti Salad
ingredientLines: 1 can (15.5-ounce) garbanzo beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place walnuts, onion, bell pepper, parsley, tuna, and garbanzo beans in a large bowl and mix lightly.
Whisk together lemon juice and olive oil and drizzle over salad; stir lightly to coat ingredients with dressing. Season with salt and pepper, if desired.
Place lettuce on a platter or divide between 8 salad bowls. Top with equal amounts of salad.
contributor: Created by the California Walnut Commission, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

title: Mixed Fruit Salad
ingredientLines: 1 can mandarin oranges, drained (in light syrup)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together.
Cover and chill until ready to serve.
Refrigerate leftovers.
contributor: Eating Smart, Being Active Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

title: Pasta Primavera Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Rinse in cold water to stop cooking and prevent sticking. Drain.
Cook vegetables until just tender. Drain and cool.
Combine cold pasta, vegetables, envelope of soup mix and salad dressing.
Top with sliced eggs and cheese.
Refrigerate until time to serve.
contributor: Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education ONIE Project

title: Pasta Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Drain and place in bowl or pan.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix well.
Cool in refrigerator before serving.
contributor: Easy and Nutritious Family Recipes University of California Cooperative Extension Fresno County

title: Pasta Salad with Herb Vinaigrette
ingredientLines: 6 ounces uncooked whole wheat pasta, cooked, drained
steps: Whisk dressing ingredients in a small bowl until blended.
Combine pasta, broccoli, tomato, and carrot in a large bowl; toss. Pour dressing over pasta mixture; toss until evenly coated. Add eggs; toss briefly.
Refrigerate, covered, at least 4 hours to blend flavors.
contributor: Meeting Your MyPlate Goals on a Budget MyPlate National Strategic Partners Toolkit

title: Pineapple Avocado Chicken Salad
ingredientLines: 2 cups cooked, cubed chicken breast (about 8 oz.)
4 6-1/2 inch whole wheat pita pockets (or 8 4-inch pita pockets)
steps: Mash 1/2 avocado in a small dish; add yogurt, rice vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Cut remaining avocado into small chunks and mix together with pineapple, bell pepper, carrots, cabbage, green onion, and chicken.
Add dressing; mix gently.
Fill pita pockets and serve.
contributor: Produce for Better Health

title: Pink Party Salad
ingredientLines: 1 cup peas, green, fresh or frozen
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil the potatoes in 2 cups of water in a deep kettle. Cover and cook over moderate heat for about 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
When thoroughly cool, dice potatoes and place in a big bowl.
Add diced beets and mix with the potatoes.
Set aside 1/4 cup of peas for garnishing and add the rest to the bowl.
Save 1 egg to use as a garnish. Chop the rest and add to the bowl.
Peel the skin off the apple and remove the core. Cut the apple into small pieces, place in a small bowl, and sprinkle with lemon juice. Add apple to the salad.
Add the vinegar, olive oil, and sugar.
Mix thoroughly. Chill and serve.
contributor: From the Farm to the Table University of Connecticut Cooperative Extension Hispanic Health Council

title: Potato Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub the potatoes, and peel them.
Cut the potatoes into 1-inch cubes.
Put the potatoes into a saucepan. Cover with water.
Bring the potatoes to a boil on medium heat.
Let the potatoes simmer for 15 minutes until they’re soft.
Drain the hot water, and let the potatoes cool.
While the potatoes are cooling, peel and chop some onions until you have 1 cup of chopped onions.
Chop the celery until you have 1/2 cup of chopped celery.
Put the chopped onion and celery in a medium mixing bowl.
Add the mayonnaise and pickle relish. Stir together.
Add the cooled potatoes. Stir again.
Cover the bowl. Put in the fridge for at least 2 hours before serving.
contributor: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

title: Potato Salad
steps: Put potatoes in a pot and cover with cold water.
Bring to a boil over high heat and cook about 15 minutes, until potatoes are tender.
Drain and set aside to cool to room temperature.
While potatoes are cooling, mix the yogurt, olive oil, and mustard in a small bowl.
Add the yogurt mixture to the cooled potatoes and gently mix.
Stir in the celery, scallions, and parsley.
Serve right away or cover and refrigerate up to 2 days.
contributor: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

title: Quick 'N Cool Summer Salad
ingredientLines: 1 can green beans, low-sodium (14.5 ounce, drained, or other vegetable)
1 can tuna packed in water (6.5 ounces, drained and flaked)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare elbow macaroni according to package directions and drain.
Add vegetables, tuna, onions, cheese, and pickles.
Mix yogurt, salad dressing, lemon juice, salt, and seasoned pepper.
Toss with macaroni mixture.
Chill before serving.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly.
contributor: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals Washington State University Extension

title: Quick and Easy Baked Potato Salad
ingredientLines: 3 tablespoons real bacon bits or pieces
steps: Place whole potatoes (do not poke holes) into microwave-safe dish.
Cover dish. (If covering dish with plastic wrap, poke small holes in plastic.)
Microwave on high for 10 to 12 minutes depending on strength of microwave.
Use oven mitts or a towel to remove dish from microwave. Carefully remove cover from dish due to steam build up and let cool.
Cut potatoes into bite-sized pieces and place in a large bowel with remaining ingredients. Stir and mix well.
contributor: Meeting Your MyPlate Goals on a Budget MyPlate National Strategic Partners Toolkit

title: Quick Black Bean Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Leave frozen corn in the fridge overnight to defrost. If you forget to do this ahead of time, defrost it in the microwave.
Drain and rinse the black beans.
Combine all ingredients together and serve as a side dish.

title: Quinoa and Black Bean Salad
ingredientLines: 1 can black beans, low-sodium (15.5 ounce can, rinsed and drained)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse the quinoa in cold water. Boil water in a saucepan, and then add the quinoa.
Return to boil, and then simmer until the water is absorbed, 10 to 15 minutes. Cool for 15 minutes.
While quinoa is cooking, mix olive oil, lime juice, cumin, coriander, chopped cilantro, and scallions in a small bowl, and set aside.
Combine chopped vegetables with the black beans in a large bowl, and set aside.
Once quinoa has cooled, combine all ingredients and mix well.
Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.
contributor: Delicious Heart-Healthy Latino Recipes/ Platillos Latinos Sabrosos y Saludables US Department of Health and Human Services National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

title: Rainbow Veggie Salad
ingredientLines: 1 can (15.5 ounces) red kidney beans, low-sodium (drained and rinsed)
1 can (15.5 ounces) black beans, low-sodium (drained and rinsed)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all the vegetables together in a large bowl.
Pour dressing over vegetables.
Sprinkle with pepper.
Stir gently, coating all vegetables.
Cover and refrigerate at least 8 hours.
contributor: 2009 Recipe Calendar University of Maryland Extension Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

title: Red Potato Salad
steps: To prepare sauce, combine yogurt, mayonnaise and mustard in a small bowl. Mix well and refrigerate.
Wash potatoes and place in pot. Cover with water about 1 inch above potatoes.
Bring water and potatoes to a boil and simmer until potatoes are fork tender.
Drain potatoes and set aside to cool.
When potatoes are cooled, cut into bite-sized cubes. Place cut potatoes into large bowl.
Add celery, onions, salt, and pepper to potatoes. Top with sauce and mix well.
Garnish with parsley and enjoy.
contributor: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

title: Roasted Chickpeas (Garbanzo Beans)
ingredientLines: 1 can (15 oz) garbanzo beans, low-sodium (drained and rinsed)
spices of your choice, optional (try garlic, paprika, sage, etc.)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Drain and rinse the beans until there is no foamy residue. Pick out the skins and discard. Wrap the drained beans in a clean towel to dry thoroughly.
Measure oil into a 9x13 baking dish or foil lined pan. Pour beans into dish, sprinkle with salt and spices. Mix oil and spices well to coat all the beans.
Bake for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring or shaking every 15 minutes. Longer makes more crunch, but watch to prevent burning!
contributor: USDA Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)

title: Salad with Pineapple, Nuts, and Raisins
ingredientLines: 1 cup vegetables (tomatoes, cucumbers, carrots, green beans) (chopped)
1 cup pineapple chunks, drained (canned in juice, or fresh orange segments)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put mixed salad greens on a large platter or in a salad bowl.
In a large bowl, mix chopped vegetables and pineapple or orange segments.
Add dressing and stir.
Spoon mixture over salad greens.
Top with raisins and nuts. Serve.
In a small bowl, mix all ingredients.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
contributor: California 5 A Day, It’s So Easy, Adapted from Oprah's Outtasight Salad Contra Costa Health Services

title: Sanchico Tuna Salad
ingredientLines: 1 can chunk light tuna (in water, 6.5 ounce can)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain tuna. Transfer to a mixing bowl and mix well with avocado for texture.
Add tomatoes, onion, pepper, lime juice, salt, and mango.
contributor: Houston Food Bank Chef Jose Montoya

title: Shrimp Confetti Salad Sandwich with Grapes
ingredientLines: 1/2 pound frozen cooked cocktail shrimp (thawed, peeled, and deveined)
1 8-oz can yellow corn kernels (no salt added, drained)
1 cup canned black beans (no salt added, drained and rinsed)
4 leaves Bibb lettuce or other leaf lettuce
steps: Chop shrimp coarsely.
Mix together shrimp salad ingredients (everything except for the bread, tomato slices, and lettuce).
Divide salad evenly among 4 slices of bread; spread to edges of bread.
Top with tomato slices, lettuce, and second bread slice.
contributor: Produce for Better Health Foundation

title: Simply Satisfying Kale and Tuna Salad
steps: Wash kale. Set aside to drain water off.
Cut tomatoes in half and lightly toss in bowl with balsamic vinegar, oil, and pinch of salt and pepper. Set aside.
In a salad bowl, mix tuna and juice from the can gently with the squeeze of 1/2 lemon and a pinch of pepper.
Massage kale for about 3 minutes to soften it.
Add the kale and 1/2 the tomatoes to the tuna. Gently toss until all is coated with dressing.
Add remaining tomatoes.
Squeeze remaining lemon all over and serve.
contributor: Seafood Nutrition Partnership

title: Snappy Cole Slaw
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and shred the cabbage with a knife or grater. Put in a mixing bowl.
Bring the vinegar and water to a boil in the saucepan. Remove from heat and add other ingredients except cabbage to the saucepan.
Continue to cook this mixture in the saucepan until the sugar is dissolved and hot, then pour over the shredded cabbage.
Toss. Refrigerate until chilled to blend flavors.
contributor: Eating Right Is Basic Michigan State University Cooperative Extension Service Nutrition Education Program

title: Somali Summer Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine oil and lemon juice.
Dice all the fruits and vegetables and then add to the bowl.
Add salt and pepper to taste (optional).
Serve chilled.
Best served within 24 hours.
contributor: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine North Dakota State University Extension Service

title: South of the Border Salad
ingredientLines: 3 cups canned corn, low sodium (drained and rinsed)
2 cans black beans, low-sodium (15.5 ounces each, drained and rinsed)
1 can diced tomatoes with green chilies (10 ounces)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the salad ingredients in a large bowl.
Mix the dressing ingredients in a small bowl.
Pour dressing over corn mixture and mix well.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
contributor: 2009 Recipe Calendar University of Maryland Extension Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

title: Spicy Cucumber & Orange Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash the cucumbers, oranges and lemon or lime under cold running water.
Slice the cucumbers. Peel and cut the oranges into small pieces.
Place cucumber slices and orange pieces in a medium size bowl. Add chili powder, lemon or lime juice and salt.
contributor: Recipe Adapted from: A Simple Mexican Salad, Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

title: Spinach Black Bean Salad
ingredientLines: 1 1/2 cups black beans, low-sodium (canned, drained, and rinsed)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine vinegar, oil, mustard, garlic, oregano, basil, and nutmeg.
Wash, drain, and chop spinach.
Add spinach, black beans, tomatoes, and onions to vinegar and oil. Toss well and serve.
contributor: Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes Connecticut Food Policy Council

title: Spinach Rice Salad
ingredientLines: 2/3 cup fresh spinach (washed and cut into thin strips)
1/2 cup thinly sliced green onion (including tops)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine dressing, soy sauce, and sugar. Stir into chilled rice.
Cover and chill salad.
Add celery, onion, and spinach before serving.
Shake on bacon bits if desired.
contributor: University of Connecticut

title: Spinach Salad with Apples and Eggs
ingredientLines: 1 cup dried figs (about 16 figs or one 7 ounce package)
1/2 cup light honey mustard or poppy seed dressing
steps: To hard boil eggs: Place eggs in saucepan large enough to hold them in a single layer. Add cold water to cover eggs by 1 inch. Heat over high heat just to boiling. Remove from heat and cover. Let eggs stand in hot water about 12 minutes. Drain and fill pan with cold water; let sit 10 to 15 minutes. Peel and slice. (If making ahead, refrigerate cooked unpeeled eggs.)
Prepare other ingredients while eggs are cooking and cooling.
Wash, slice, and core apples.
Cut apples and dried figs into bite-sized chunks.
Wash and drain spinach.
To plate, divide ingredients evenly among four plates, top spinach with apples, eggs, dried figs, and croutons. Drizzle with dressing
contributor: Produce for Better Health Foundation

title: Spinach Salad with Apples and Raisins
ingredientLines: 1 package baby spinach, 10 ounces, washed (or kale or other greens)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine spinach, apples, and raisins.
Mix all dressing ingredients and pour over salad just prior to serving.
contributor: Eat Smart. Be Fit. University of Maryland Extension

title: Splendid Fruit Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix yogurt, cinnamon, and orange juice in a medium bowl.
Wash and chop the fruit and add
to the yogurt mixture. Stir and serve.
contributor: Iowa Department of Public Health Iowa Nutrition Network

title: Summer Fruit Salad
ingredientLines: 1 cup pineapple chunks, fresh or canned packed in natural juice (do not drain)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Stir fruit together in a medium-sized bowl.
Cover and chill. Serve as soon as possible.
contributor: University of Nebraska-Lincoln Cooperative Extension

title: Summer Salad
steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Wash and dry greens. Tear into bite-sized pieces and place in large salad bowl.
Add onion, mushrooms, walnuts, and parsley. Just before serving, toss with dressing.
contributor: Creative Vegetable Cookery North Dakota State University Extension Service

title: Sunshine Salad
ingredientLines: 5 cups spinach leaves (packed, washed, and dried well)
2 oranges (peeled and chopped into bite-sized pieces)
1/3 cup vinaigrette dressing ("lite" -- around 15 calories per tablespoon or less)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss all ingredients together in a large bowl. Add dressing and toss again.
Serve immediately.
contributor: US Department of Health and Human Services

title: Sweet Potato Harvest Salad
ingredientLines: 4 cups sweet potatoes, diced (about 2-3 sweet potatoes)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Drizzle diced sweet potatoes with 1 teaspoon of olive oil and roast in the oven on a baking sheet for 10 minutes.
Once sweet potatoes are cooked, remove from the oven and allow them to cool.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the sweet potato, apples, pomegranate seeds, and pepitas.
Whisk the remaining 1/2 tablespoon of olive oil, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper in a separate bowl.
Once mixed, add to sweet potato mixture and toss until the salad is lightly coated.
contributor: Created by Brighter Bites, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

title: Taco Salad
ingredientLines: 3 cups lettuce (use butterhead or any other head of lettuce, torn into small pieces)
16 ounces ground turkey or ground beef
1 can pinto beans, low-sodium (15 1/2 ounce, drained)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put lettuce in large bowl. Add tomatoes and green pepper.
Brown meat and onion in fry pan. Drain off fat and liquid.
Mix meat, beans, and salsa. Add to salad mixture.
Serve with additional salsa. Refrigerate leftovers.
contributor: Simply Good Eating Recipe Cards, Vol. 1, 2000 University of Minnesota Cooperative Extension Service

title: Taco Salad II
ingredientLines: 1 cup kidney or pinto beans (dry-cooked or canned, drained)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef and drain any fat.
Add beans, cumin, and chili powder and heat through.
Toss lettuce, tomatoes, onion, and cheese in large bowl.
Spoon on meat and bean mixture and top with broken tortilla chips.
Prepare dressing by mixing yogurt and salsa. Serve on the side of the salad
Refrigerate leftovers within two hours.
contributor: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals Washington State University Extension

title: Tangy Crisp Vegetable and Pasta Salad
ingredientLines: 1/2 cup pasta (such as bowties, shells, macaroni, etc.)
1/2 red pepper (sliced, could use green or yellow)
1 tablespoon dried parsley (can use fresh if available)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions, but do not add salt to cooking water.
Drain, rinse with cool water, and drain again.
In a small saucepan, combine vinegar, sugar, garlic powder, and black pepper.
Stir over medium heat until sugar is dissolved, but do not boil. Let cool.
Rinse, drain, and chop remaining ingredients. Combine in a shallow container.
Add cooked pasta and vinegar mixture. Mix gently.
Cover and refrigerate overnight to allow flavors to blend.
Top with parsley and serve cold.
Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
contributor: Fix it Fresh! Recipe Series Kansas State University Research and Extension

title: The Perfect "Pear" and Brussels Sprout Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large mixing bowl, add the pear, Brussels sprouts, and all other ingredients and mix until well incorporated.
Serve and enjoy!
contributor: Created by Brighter Bites, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

title: Three Bean Salad
ingredientLines: 1 cup green beans, cut (canned or fresh cooked)
2 cups yellow wax beans (canned or fresh cooked)
1/4 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix beans, vegetables and garlic cloves in a large bowl.
Mix vinegar, oil, and sugar in a saucepan. Heat until sugar dissolves. Cool slightly.
Stir seasonings into vinegar mixture. Pour over vegetables. Toss lightly. Chill overnight.
Remove garlic before serving.
contributor: The Bold and Beautiful Book of Bean Recipes Washington State WIC Program

title: Tofu Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

Prepare tofu by draining the water from the package and placing tofu between two plates. Put a heavy object on top and let stand for 10 to 15 minutes. Drain the water that collects on the bottom plate every few minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the mayonnaise, mustard, and soy sauce.
In a medium bowl, combine the diced tofu, celery, onion, pepper, and parley; stir in the mayonnaise mixture and toss gently to coat.
Refrigerate covered until the flavors are blended -- at least one hour.
Use as a sandwich filling or on top of whole grain crackers.
contributor: University of Connecticut Family Nutrition Program Senior Nutrition Awareness Project (SNAP) Newsletters

title: Tomato and Cucumber Salad
ingredientLines: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or oil of your choice)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine the salad ingredients.
In a small bowl, mix the dressing ingredients together.
Pour the dressing over the salad. Mix well.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
contributor: University of Nebraska at Lincoln Nebraska Nutrition Education Program

title: Tomato Basil and Bean Pasta Salad
ingredientLines: 1 pound pasta (ziti, bow tie or other shaped pasta)
2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
1 cup kidney beans (cooked or low-sodium canned drained, or try garbanzo beans or black beans)
mozzarella cheese, fat-free (cubed or shredded cheese optional)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain and cool.
In a small mixing bowl, whisk together vegetable oil, vinegar, Dijon-style mustard, and pepper to make vinaigrette.
In a large mixing bowl, combine pasta, beans, basil, and tomatoes. Pour vinaigrette over top and toss together. Cover and chill at least 1 hour.
If desired, add nuts and cheese just before serving, tossing again to combine.
contributor: Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes Connecticut Food Policy Council

title: Tuna Apple Salad
ingredientLines: 1 can tuna, packed in water (12 ounces)
2 pita bread, whole wheat (cut in half)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, stir together tuna, onion, apple, celery, raisins, and 2 tablespoons of dressing.
In another bowl, toss together salad greens with remaining dressing.
Carefully open pita breads and fill with equal amounts of greens and tuna salad.
contributor: Discover the Secret to Healthy Living California Department of Health Services California Children’s 5-A-Day Power Play Campaign

title: Tuna Apple Salad Sandwich
ingredientLines: 1 apple (such as Fuji or Pink Lady Washington)
8 leaves lettuce (Bibb, Romaine, green, or red leaf)
steps: Cut apple in quarters; remove core and chop.
In a medium-sized bowl, mix all salad ingredients, except tuna.
Gently fold in tuna.
Make sandwiches using lettuce and whole-grain bread (toasted, if desired), and fill with tuna apple salad.
contributor: Produce for Better Health Foundation

title: Tuna Salad with Grapes
ingredientLines: 2 cans water packed tuna (5 ounce cans, drained)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine drained tuna, celery, mayonnaise and yogurt and stir.
Add grapes to mixture and stir gently.
Cover and chill until ready to serve.
Serve over lettuce leaves.
contributor: Eating Smart, Being Active Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

title: Turkey Potato Salad
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix turkey, celery, potato, onion, and green pepper.
Mix mayonnaise, mustard and salt. Stir lightly into turkey mixture.
Chill.
contributor: University of Maine Cooperative Extension

title: Turkey Salad with Orange Vinaigrette
ingredientLines: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or oil of your choice)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

In a jar with tight-fitting lid, combine all vinaigrette ingredients; shake well. If you don't have a container with a tight-fitting lid, place ingredients in a small mixing bowl and mix together with a whisk.
In large bowl, combine all salad ingredients; toss gently.
Serve with vinaigrette.
contributor: Cook it QUICK! University of Nebraska Cooperative Extension

title: Vegetable Salad
ingredientLines: 1 can whole kernel corn (15 ounce, drained)
1 can diced tomatoes (reserve 1/3 cup liquid), low-sodium
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain corn, carrots, and chickpeas. Throw away liquid. Rinse vegetables and drain again.
Drain tomatoes but save 1/3 cup of the liquid.
Mix corn, carrots, chickpeas, tomatoes, onion, and green pepper in a large bowl.
Mix together all other ingredients in a separate bowl.
Pour over vegetables.
Cover and set aside for at least 3 hours in the refrigerator.
contributor: University of Wyoming Cooperative Extension

title: Vidalia Onion and Tomato Salad with Grilled Tuna
ingredientLines: 1/2 pound ahi (yellowfin) tuna steak (fresh or frozen)
1 large head lettuce (Boston, Romaine or Bibb) (washed, dried, and torn into bite-sized pieces)
1/4 cup lemon juice, fresh or bottled
steps: Heat grill.
Whisk together dressing ingredients in a small bowl.
Cut tuna into 1-inch chunks and skewer and place on two or three 3-inch skewers; brush lightly with olive oil. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Grill skewered tuna until fish is opaque and flakes with a fork (145 °F); remove from grill.
In a large bowl, toss dressing with all vegetable ingredients. To serve, divide salad on four individual plates; top with tuna.
contributor: Produce for Better Health Foundation

title: Zesty Citrus Coleslaw
ingredientLines: 4 cups shredded cabbage (16 ounce bag of coleslaw mix)
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix together the coleslaw mix, peanuts (if using), and Mandarin oranges in a large bowl.
Stir in the Italian salad dressing and soy sauce.
contributor: 2009 Recipe Calendar University of Maryland Extension Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

title: Zesty Pasta Primavera Salad
ingredientLines: 2 cups whole grain rotini pasta, uncooked*
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to the package directions.
Drain and set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk oil, lemon juice, Italian seasoning, and red pepper flakes.
Add cooked pasta, cucumber, tomato, carrots, red onion, and Parmesan cheese to the dressing.
Mix well and chill for 2 hours before serving.
contributor: Recipe adapted from Chickasaw Nation Get Fresh! Nutrition Education Program
